title: Other (Please Specify), Explained
subtitle: Halvard Nnamani on what becomes of the words typed into the last box on a community organisation's online form
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Halvard Nnamani's doctoral thesis about the "Other (please specify)" box on community organisations' online forms. It follows a parent's registration from the box into the organisation's files, sets the census and the trace beside the thesis's three-arm trial, and closes on the rule the University has adopted for its own forms. Nnamani describes the work in his own words.
topic: A research explainer of the doctoral thesis following what is typed into the "Other (please specify)" box on community organisations' online forms, through a census of 61,208 entries, a trace of each box through its keeper's files, recorded form-filling sessions and a three-arm retention trial, finding that the box matters and its contents do not

beats.text: Text typed into that box is not transmitted from the respondent’s device, is not stored, and appears in no export. The box is rendered, not retained.
The box does its work at the moment of typing. It's a courtesy the form extends to the person filling it in.
